# CANDIDATE: MIDDAY_RIBBON_FADE_RSI_EXTREME_SHORT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Extended overbought RSI readings (>80) occurring alongside a bullish EMA ribbon (EMA8 > EMA21 > EMA34) and price above VWAP often precede a mean-reversion pullback, offering a short opportunity. The pattern captures intraday exhaustion in low‑volatility regimes (VIX < 20) when the market is prone to snap‑backs after extended momentum.

## Mechanism

**Entry:** On the 5‑minute chart, require three consecutive bars where RSI(14) > 80, price is above VWAP, and the ribbon is bullish (EMA8 > EMA21 > EMA34). Enter a short at the close of the third bar.  
**Exit:** Initial stop is placed above the highest high of the three‑bar sequence (or the opening‑range high if higher). TP1 is set at 1× risk (distance from entry to stop). A runner is trailed using either a premium‑stop of 0.5 % of the entry price or a chart‑stop triggered when price crosses back above VWAP, whichever occurs first. Trading is restricted to 10:30 ET–14:00 ET, avoiding the first and last 30 minutes, and only when VIX < 20.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** The strategy assumes a $25K+ account to accommodate the default qty of 28 contracts (ITM‑2 strikes) under the 50% per‑trade risk cap; a $1K paper account would realize roughly 14% of headline P&L.
2. **Sample bias:** The concept is derived from intraday price action principles and has not yet been backtested on any historical sample; thus sample size is zero and overfit risk is high until a Stage‑1 grinder evaluation is performed.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no walk‑forward or held‑out window has been evaluated).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (no realistic OPRA fill simulation has been run on the top three J days).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst‑case scenario involves a strong trending day where RSI remains >80 for extended periods, causing repeated stop‑outs; max drawdown could exceed 30% of account equity if the stop is hit repeatedly without a mean‑reversion bounce; blow‑up risk arises if the premium‑stop fails to trigger and the runner accumulates large adverse moves during a breakdown.
6. **Concentration:** Unknown until a Stage‑1 backtest is completed; the hypothesis suggests the edge may be dispersed across many low‑volatility days, but concentration disclosure will be provided post‑backtest.
